title: Tracing sidecar producer with adaptive exporter failover and per-tenant routing
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Summary: Build a lightweight tracing sidecar (producer) that buffers and enriches spans locally, routes them to the optimal backend per-tenant (jaeger, tempo, or third-party), and implements adaptive exporter failover with backoff and secondary queues. Background: Current deployment relies on app-instrumented OTLP exporters that push directly to our ingest layer. We see transient failures and cross-tenant noisy exporters causing latency spikes and dropped spans. Goals: 1) Reduce application-level span drops by introducing a local producer with retry/queueing and granular per-tenant routing. 2) Provide adaptive exporter failover: primary -> secondary -> local durable storage (S3) path when cluster exports are unhealthy. 3) Offer observability for producer health, queue/backpressure, and per-tenant success rates. Non-goals: Full feature parity with collector SDKs (this is a pragmatic producer focused on reliability and routing). Design proposal: - Sidecar runs as a tiny Go binary alongside services (k8s DaemonSet/sidecar pattern) exposing OTLP/grpc and HTTP endpoints. - Incoming spans are enriched with runtime metadata (pod, region, customer_id) based on env/cgroup. - Routing config: per-tenant routing table stored in centralized config (ConfigMap/Console-managed) mapping tenant -> preferred backend (tempo/jaeger/third). - Exporter pipeline: write-ahead buffer (in-memory FIFO with configurable soft/hard limits) -> batcher -> exporter. Exporter implements adaptive failover: on repeated 5xx/timeout the exporter marks backend degraded and switches to configured secondary; if all backends degraded for >15m, sidecar archives batches to S3-compatible bucket and emits an alert. - Backpressure: when soft limit reached, sidecar applies sampling policies (drop low-priority spans) and emits metrics. Monitoring & dashboards: add Grafana panels for queue depth, export success rate, per-tenant error rate, exporter latency p95/p99. Acceptance criteria: - Sidecar accepts OTLP payloads and successfully routes to configured backends in canary cluster. - Under injected failures (simulated backend 500s), sidecar flips to secondary and persists to durable store after threshold. - End-to-end latency for application requests increases by <2ms on average. - New dashboards show queue depth and per-tenant export success with alerting rules. Rollout plan: 1) Internal dev canary on staging services for 2 weeks. 2) Opt-in beta for 10 internal customers (platform teams) with console toggle. 3) Gradual ramp to all services, monitor SLOs and telemetry for 48h per batch. Testing: unit tests for exporter state machine, fault injection integration test, perf benchmark with 1k span/sec. Docs: Confluence design doc and runbook, sample k8s manifests, and migration guide for ops teams.
